owner.name: NASA - National Aeronautics and Space Administration

title: NASA Astronaut Chris Williams: Thinking Like a Scientist
transcript:
I remember really well the first time
realizing that you could use math and science and technology
and laws of the universe to figure out how things work and kind of making
that connection in my head, I think was was pretty special for me
and kind of led me down the path, that I've traveled
through the rest of my career. Chris! What's up? How’s it going? Dude! I'm so happy to see you guys. Oh, how's it going, Johnny? It's great to see you. Welcome to the USOS segment, bud. Feels just like Building 9. I'm a scientist by background. I'm a physicist. But, I have done up here all sorts of different biology experiments,
some chemistry experiments, experiments on the human body,
and things like growing plants. All things that are different because
there are scientists on the ground that came up with really good ideas
that we can help, figure out and help them answer questions about. I was doing a bunch of biology experiments
just last week in a glove box, and I'd never done that before,
but knowing that I know how to think like a scientist. And I've learned how to
think like a scientist gave me the confidence to say, okay, well, this isn't something I've done before,
but I know how to approach these problems. But the biggest skill is teamwork. That's how we get
these incredible things done. Chris, it was awesome to watch you and Jessica
go out on a spacewalk. You know, it's been an incredible time
getting to, be here on, station. I think we've done a really great job here
of proving out some of the technologies that we're going to use
as we take our next exploration steps. One of the things that I found
the most interesting is how varied and different
the skills are to be successful on a mission
to the International Space Station. You really have to execute at a high level
and you kind of prove to yourself that you can do it. You can do a whole lot more
than maybe you think you can.
